explanations.A_A: Both the mother and father have Type A blood. Each can provide either the dominant I^A allele or a recessive i allele. Children therefore inherit I^A from both parents (Type A) or receive i from both parents, producing Type O if each parent carries the recessive allele.
explanations.A_B: The mother is Type A and the father is Type B. Each provides a dominant allele (I^A or I^B) or a recessive i. Children may inherit I^A I^B (Type AB), I^A i (Type A), I^B i (Type B), or ii (Type O) if both contribute the recessive allele, so all four phenotypes are possible.
explanations.A_AB: The mother is Type A (I^A I^A or I^A i) and the father is Type AB (I^A I^B). Offspring always receive either I^A or I^B from the father and I^A or i from the mother. That yields Type A (I^A I^A or I^A i) or Type AB (I^A I^B), but never Type B or O because the AB parent never contributes i.
explanations.A_O: Mother Type A carries at least one I^A allele, while the father is Type O (ii). Every child receives i from the father and either I^A or i from the mother, producing Type A (I^A i) or Type O (ii). Type B and AB cannot appear because the O parent lacks the I^B allele.
explanations.B_A: Mother Type B and father Type A create the same possibilities as an A × B cross. Dominant alleles from either parent can combine to form Type AB, and recessive combinations can produce Type O. Thus, children may be Type A, Type B, Type AB, or Type O.
explanations.B_B: Both parents are Type B. Each can pass along the dominant I^B allele or a recessive i. Children who receive I^B from at least one parent are Type B; those who inherit i from both parents become Type O. Type A or AB cannot appear because no I^A allele is available.
explanations.B_AB: The mother is Type B (I^B I^B or I^B i) and the father is Type AB (I^A I^B). Children always get I^A or I^B from the father and I^B or i from the mother. That combination produces either Type AB (I^A I^B) or Type B (I^B I^B or I^B i); Type A and O are impossible.
explanations.B_O: With a Type B mother and Type O father, every child receives i from the father and either I^B or i from the mother. This yields Type B (I^B i) or Type O (ii). Type A and AB cannot result because the B parent does not provide an I^A allele.
explanations.AB_A: A Type AB mother always contributes either I^A or I^B, while a Type A father contributes I^A or i. Children therefore become Type A (I^A I^A or I^A i) when the AB parent passes I^A, or Type AB when she contributes I^B and the father supplies I^A.
explanations.AB_B: A Type AB mother paired with a Type B father produces children that are either Type B (I^B I^B or I^B i) or Type AB (I^A I^B). The AB parent cannot supply a recessive i, so Type O never occurs, and Type A requires an I^A from both sides which the B parent cannot provide.
explanations.AB_AB: When both parents are Type AB, every child inherits one allele from each parent that is either I^A or I^B. The combinations are I^A I^A (Type A), I^A I^B (Type AB), or I^B I^B (Type B). Type O cannot appear because neither parent carries the recessive i allele.
explanations.AB_O: A Type AB mother and Type O father can only produce Type A or Type B offspring. The O parent always supplies i, while the AB parent supplies either I^A or I^B, resulting in I^A i (Type A) or I^B i (Type B). Neither AB nor O is possible because the O parent lacks dominant alleles and the AB parent lacks a recessive allele.
explanations.O_A: Mother Type O (ii) and father Type A (I^A I^A or I^A i) give children who always receive i from the mother and I^A or i from the father. The results are Type A (I^A i) or Type O (ii). Types B and AB are impossible without an I^B allele.
explanations.O_B: Mother Type O provides only i alleles, while a Type B father supplies I^B or i. Offspring therefore become Type B (I^B i) or Type O (ii). Type A and AB cannot occur because the parents do not pass along an I^A allele.
explanations.O_AB: A Type O mother can only contribute i alleles, and a Type AB father provides either I^A or I^B. Children inherit I^A i (Type A) or I^B i (Type B). Type AB is impossible because the mother never supplies a dominant allele, and Type O fails because the father never supplies i.
explanations.O_O: Both parents are Type O (ii), so every child must inherit i from each parent, resulting only in Type O offspring.
